sealed.works: Closest to the product: a payment that stays sealed until the recipient opens it, and it ties to QoreSeal, the encrypted notice. The coral seal is the one element that reads as 'the money'.
sealed.risks: An envelope is the universal mail icon, so next to a wallet or an inbox it can read as 'messages', not 'payments'. Says nothing about refunds or quantum safety.
sealed.small: At 16px it holds as a rectangle with a dot; the flap lines thin out. Legible, but generic.

return.works: The only mark that is also the letter, so the symbol and the wordmark are one idea. One continuous stroke tells the refund story: it goes out, and if nobody claims it, it comes back.
return.risks: The looped tail can read as a speech bubble or a map pin if drawn too round; the loop must stay slim. Quantum safety is not in the mark, it lives in the product.
return.small: Best at 16px: a ring with a tail is a Q at any size, and a single stroke has nothing to fill in.

lattice.works: The most honest quantum-safe reference (ML-DSA is lattice cryptography) and the square-cut wordmark has real character. The coral cell is a clear 'one payment moves'.
lattice.risks: A 3×3 grid of squares is the 'all apps' launcher icon and a phone keypad; most senders will not know what a lattice is, so the meaning needs explaining. Feels technical rather than calm.
lattice.small: At 16px the nine cells blur into a grey square with a coral dot; it survives as a shape, not as a lattice.
